scope: First flagship 1529–1540 historical research, not production code

researchFindings.description: German Article 15 has shared Eucharistic assertions (gaistliche niessung), records nonagreement concerning leiblich im Brot und wein, and exhorts charity. GHDI source is edited from WA 30/III, not manuscript autopsy.
Gruber 46 records 1531 Latin Wittenberg Georg Rhau; Gruber 7 has November 1531 German colophon; Pitts 2017 independent German Wittenberg Georg Rhau object has VD16 C4736.

Gruber 28 and Pitts independently identify 1540 Variata. Pitts catalogue identifies VD16 C4713. Article X change reported as vere adsint et distribuantur versus cum pane et vino vere exhibeantur in later scholarly transcriptions; no direct page-by-page collation.

Gruber explicitly describes a different 1540 copy as not Variata but does not present an unambiguous standalone Gruber number in the paragraph. C4713 belongs to Pitts Variata and must not be assigned to Gruber non-Variata.
1540 title Addita est Apologia Confessionis diligenter recognita grammatically marks the Apology revised, not the Augsburg Confession; the latter's Variata status requires independent evidence.
Calvinists compromise and broader confession reception are modern catalogue or confessional historical framing, not contemporary self-description or full doctrinal acceptance evidence.
